answer: BioGuard AI is a QA automation portfolio project. It tests a fictional lab app that scores samples as PASS or REVIEW. All data is made up.
The tests use Playwright with TypeScript. It also uses Docker, GitHub Actions, Jenkins and an optional local AI called Ollama.
A sample with signal quality of 0.80 or more is PASS. Anything lower is REVIEW, so a person checks it.
The user pages are tested in three browser engines: Chromium for Chrome and Edge, Firefox, and WebKit for Safari.
The API tests check the sample data, reject bad input with an error, and make sure every change is written to an audit log.
After six wrong passwords the account locks and a six digit code is emailed. The tests read that code from a fake inbox called Mailpit.
The QC report PDF is downloaded and compared with an approved copy: the text, the numbers from the API, and a picture of the page.
You can upload a CSV file of samples. The tests check good files, and bad files like missing values, wrong headers and duplicate IDs.
Every test is linked to a requirement with a risk level. The dashboard shows which requirements passed.
GitHub Actions runs all tests every day and publishes a dashboard to GitHub Pages. Jenkins can run the same pipeline too.
With Docker Desktop running, one command starts the app, the fake inbox and the tests. You do not need to install Node or Playwright.
A local AI suggests new test ideas and explains failed tests. A person must approve every suggestion, and AI never decides if a test passes.
The project has switches that plant bugs on purpose, to prove the tests catch them. The tests also found a real cookie bug in Safari.
It was built by Swetha, a senior QA automation engineer, as a portfolio project.
